title: Archiving Files on the Command Line

sections.title: Mission · Archive, Compress, and Extract
paragraphs: Linux administrators frequently need to package files together, compress them, move them, back them up, or extract them later. The central distinction is archiving versus compression.

sections.title: Archive vs. Compression
paragraphs: An archive combines files or directories into one container. Compression reduces the storage space data requires. A file can be archived without compression, and an archive can also be compressed.

sections.title: tar · Tape Archive
paragraphs: tar is one of the most important Linux archiving utilities. Its name comes from tape archive, but it now commonly packages files and directories regardless of whether tape is involved. notes.txt, report.txt, and project/ can become backup.tar.

sections.callout: C = CREATE · X = EXTRACT · F = FILE · V = VERBOSE

sections.title: Creating a tar Archive
paragraphs: tar -cf backup.tar Documents/ creates backup.tar from Documents/. The c creates, f says the archive filename follows, backup.tar is the result, and Documents/ is the content.

sections.title: Inspecting a tar Archive
paragraphs: tar -tf backup.tar lists the archive's contents without extracting them. When gzip is involved, tar -tzf backup.tar.gz lists the compressed archive. The t operation means list or inspect.
sections.callout: INSPECT WITHOUT EXTRACTING = tar -tf · GZIP ARCHIVE = tar -tzf

sections.title: Extracting a tar Archive
paragraphs: tar -xf backup.tar extracts the archive. The x means extract and f identifies the specified archive file.

sections.title: gzip
paragraphs: gzip is a compression utility. A gzip-compressed file commonly uses .gz, such as notes.txt.gz. A gzip-compressed tar archive commonly uses .tar.gz or .tgz.

sections.title: tar + gzip
paragraphs: tar uses -z for gzip compression. tar -czf backup.tar.gz Documents/ creates and gzip-compresses the archive; tar -xzf backup.tar.gz extracts it.

sections.title: bzip2
paragraphs: bzip2 is another compression utility. It uses .bz2, while a tar archive compressed with bzip2 commonly uses .tar.bz2. tar commonly uses -j for bzip2.

sections.title: xz
paragraphs: xz is another compression format and tool. It uses .xz, while a compressed tar archive may use .tar.xz. tar commonly uses uppercase -J for xz.

sections.title: Exam Trap · tar Compression Options
sections.callout: z = GZIP · j = BZIP2 · J = XZ

sections.title: zip
paragraphs: zip can package and compress files into a .zip archive. zip archive.zip file1 file2 is the basic pattern. ZIP is widely used across operating systems.

sections.title: unzip
paragraphs: unzip extracts ZIP archives. For example, unzip archive.zip opens the archive.
sections.callout: ZIP = PACK IT · UNZIP = OPEN IT

sections.title: Exam Trap · tar vs. gzip
paragraphs: tar is primarily archiving. gzip is compression. Together, .tar.gz means archived and compressed. Do not automatically say tar itself means compression.

sections.title: gzip vs. bzip2 vs. xz
paragraphs: All three are compression technologies. The exam can test the tool or extension rather than deep compression theory.
